test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Nov 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Mr. Ramesh and / his friends / have never come / here
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e. **'have never come'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment** 'have never come' **contains a grammatical error in the sentence. The subject of this sentence is "Mr. Ramesh and his friends", which is plural.
 
• In English grammar, plural subjects require plural verbs. However, the rule changes when plural subjects are connected using "and", and it is taken as a collective noun or a single entity.
 
• **In this case,** "Mr. Ramesh and his friends" is acting as a singular subject (as a group) rather than multiple individuals. Therefore, a singular verb should be used.
 
• The **correct form** of the verb would be** 'has'** and not 'have', which agrees with the singular subject. Therefore, the corrected segment would read as 'has never come'.

Therefore, the **correct sentence is: '***Mr. Ramesh and his friends **has never come** here.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'Mr. Ramesh and': **This segment is grammatically correct. It is the first part of a compound subject connected by 'and'.
 
• **'His friends': **This segment is also grammatically correct and completes the compound subject begun in the first segment.
 
• **'Here':** This segment is grammatically correct. It acts as an adverb providing location context to the action of coming.
